'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Russian military intervention in the Syrian civil war]]
***The [[Syrian opposition|rebel]]-held city of [[Idlib]] loses its supply of water after [[Russian Air Force]] jets bombed a nearby water station. Airstrikes have increased in the past 24 hours with attacks also reported on farms near the [[Bab al-Hawa Border Crossing]], and on [[Internally displaced person|IDP camps]] near [[Jisr al-Shughur]] which killed three people. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/russian-jets-bomb-rebel-held-idlib-syria-witnesses-say-2022-01-02/ (Reuters)]
*[[Switzerland|Swiss]] newspaper ''[[Neue Zürcher Zeitung]]'' reports that [[Mossad]] was responsible for three bombings of [[Germany|German]] and Swiss firms in 1981 to try to halt [[Iran and weapons of mass destruction|Iranian]] and [[Pakistan and weapons of mass destruction|Pakistani development of nuclear weapons]]. [https://www.jpost.com/international/article-691435 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2022 Parliament of South Africa fire]]
**A fire breaks out in the [[South Africa]]n [[Houses of Parliament, Cape Town|parliament building]] in [[Cape Town]], destroying its roof and the wing housing the [[National Council of Provinces]]. A man has been arrested in connection with the incident. [https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20220102-fire-breaks-out-at-south-african-parliament-building-in-cape-town (France 24)]
*[[February 13–17, 2021 North American winter storm]], [[2021 Texas power crisis]]
**The death toll from a destructive winter storm that triggered statewide blackouts in [[Texas]], U.S., last year is updated to 246. [https://www.texastribune.org/2022/01/02/texas-winter-storm-final-death-toll-246/amp/ (''The Texas Tribune'')]
*Eight people are killed and 19 injured after a heavy-duty tanker semi-trailer collided with a bus in [[Sichuan Province]], [[China]]. [https://english.news.cn/20220102/cefb270460064cc9953433abbf3053f0/c.html (Xinhua)]
*A magnitude 5.4 [[list of earthquakes in China|earthquake]] strikes on the border between [[Yunnan]] and [[Sichuan]], [[China]], injuring 22 people. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/1/2/twenty-two-people-injured-in-southwest-china-quake (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria]]
***[[Bulgaria]] reports its first 12 cases of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant]] in five [[COVID-19 vaccination in Bulgaria|vaccinated]] people and seven unvaccinated people, most of whom had not travelled abroad. [https://www.metro.us/bulgaria-detects-first-cases/ (''Metro'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[United States Secretary of Defense]] [[Lloyd Austin]] announces that he has tested positive for [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.politico.com/amp/news/2022/01/02/pentagon-lloyd-austin-covid-526376 (''Politico'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic on cruise ships]]
***[[AIDAnova]], a [[cruise ship]] operated by German cruise line [[AIDA Cruises]] and carrying 4,197 people, has docked in [[Lisbon]], [[Portugal]], after 52 crew members tested positive for COVID-19 and isolated at various hotels. [https://www.nytimes.com/2022/01/01/world/a-crew-outbreak-halts-a-german-new-years-cruise-in-lisbon.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**A [[South Korea|South Korean]] citizen crosses the heavily fortified [[Korean Demilitarized Zone]] in a rare case of [[South Korean defectors|defection]] to [[North Korea]] from the South. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-59851097 (BBC News)]
*[[Ethiopia–United States relations]], [[Guinea–United States relations]], [[Mali–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] cuts off [[Ethiopia]], [[Guinea]] and [[Mali]] from the [[African Growth and Opportunity Act]] trade preference program citing their [[human rights]] abuses and anti-democratic actions. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/1/2/us-removes-ethiopia-mali-and-guinea-from-agoa-trade-programme (Al Jazeera)]
